incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended: s. 12 (incorporation), s. 13 (articles of incorporation), s. 15.1 (unlimited liability company designation and no-par-value share requirement), s. 16 (certificate of incorporation), s. 101 (by-laws), and the associated unlimited liability company forms and fees regulations under the ABCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta; online portal at alberta.ca/corporate-registry; filings may be effectuated directly or through authorized Alberta corporate registry service providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation, accompanied by the Notice of Registered Office, the Notice of Directors, and the NUANS corporate name search report, each prescribed under the ABCA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta ULC; the articles must authorize shares without par value. No escrow, capital deposit, or bank confirmation is required at incorporation. The first directors may set the initial paid-up capital by board resolution, commonly at CAD 1 per subscription share.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [•] UNLIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, adopted this [•] day of [•], 20[•], by written consent of all directors pursuant to the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscription of [•] no-par-value unlimited liability shares by the initial shareholders is approved; allotment and issuance are ratified and the secretary shall update the securities register. 2. The registered office is established at [•], Alberta, and shall be recorded with the Alberta Corporate Registry. 3. [•] is appointed President, [•] Secretary, and [•] Treasurer, each to serve until resignation or removal. ALL OF WHICH IS RESOLVED AND RECORDED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / authorized NUANS search house via Corporate Registry Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for up to three proposed corporate names. Ensure the required legal element for an unlimited liability company is included exactly as 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'. Reserve the approved name, if desired, for up to 90 days and retain the reservation number. Use the confirmed NUANS report in the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form
Three proposed corporate names with search logic
Identity and contact details of the incorporator
Name reservation fee receipt (if reservation is requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a revised NUANS search with alternative names or submit trademark/common-law use evidence to Corporate Registry for reconsideration; obtain a waiver only where the proposed name is inherently distinctive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator(s) and legal counsel; signatures witnessed (notarization only where foreign law requires legalization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft ABCA Form 1 Articles of Incorporation containing the ULC clause under section 15.1 (shareholders jointly and severally liable for the corporation's debts and liabilities), the no-par-value share class, the Alberta registered office address, the number of first directors, and any restrictions on business. Have each incorporator sign and the witness attest the signature. Complete Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 3 (Notice of Directors) with each director's consent to act.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (signed and witnessed)
Form 2 Notice of Registered Office and occupant consent
Form 3 Notice of Directors with signed consents to act
NUANS report and reservation number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the articles are deficient, amend and re-execute the relevant schedules and resubmit within the registry's 15-day deficiency correction window to avoid a fresh filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Corporate Registry Online or in-person counters)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and NUANS report through Corporate Registry Online or an authorized service provider. Select standard (5 business days) or expedited (2 business days) service and pay the prescribed filing fee (CAD 100 standard / CAD 250 expedited). Retain the file number, payment receipt, and submission confirmation for the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Completed Forms 1, 2 and 3
NUANS report with reservation
Filing fee payment receipt
Authorization letter of the filing agent (if filing by service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency notice, provide corrected filings and pay the correction fee before the deadline; for name objections, supply a fresh NUANS report and reserved name or choose an alternate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and CRA Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (certificate issuance); Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online (1-800-959-5525)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation with the corporate file number and Corporate Access Number (CAN) from Corporate Registry. Register the corporation with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain the Business Number, including the federal corporate income tax account and, if applicable, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts. Open the corporate minute book with the certificate and file numbers recorded.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate file number and CAN
Director information and Alberta registered address
CRA Business Registration (RC1 or online) data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Number application is queried, confirm the Corporate Registry data matches CRA records, then telephone CRA Business Inquiries or resubmit the RC1; if the certificate contains typographical errors, apply for a corrected certificate under the ABCA at minimal cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors (acting under ABCA s. 101; written resolution in lieu of meeting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or pass the unanimous written First Board Resolution (text set out above). Approve the subscription and allotment of unlimited liability shares; ratify the registered office address; appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer; adopt the corporate by-laws; approve the form of share certificate; authorize the opening of the corporate bank account and signatory schedule; instruct the corporate accountant to establish the paid-up capital ledger.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (unanimous written consent)
Approved by-laws
Share subscription agreements and payment evidence
Share certificates and securities register
Bank account authorization and officer appointment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable for the meeting, circulate a written resolution in lieu of meeting signed by all directors; if quorum is lost, reconvene with substitute directors appointed by the incorporator.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; provincial registry: Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta King's Printer), accessible via ALIS or third-party service providers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Alberta ULC, incorporate through the Alberta Corporate Registry (or Corporations Canada if federal extra-provincial registration is desired) to obtain a legal entity certificate. Subsequently, the entity must register with the CRA through the Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (or by paper form RC1) to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN), a Corporate Income Tax account (RT), and a GST/HST account (RT). The BN is issued immediately upon successful online application; paper applications typically take 2–4 weeks. Non-resident directors or officers must provide a Canadian address for service and certified identification. Once incorporated, the ULC has a separate legal personality and is a resident of Canada for tax purposes; therefore, the BN number is the statutory TIN for all federal tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (For Canadian income tax purposes, the ULC is an entity-level taxable corporation subject to Part I corporate income tax; however, due to its unlimited liability character, it may be treated as a disregarded entity or partnership for US federal tax purposes if a check-the-box election is made. The entity structure is Pass_Through_Eligible only in the cross-border sense, not under domestic Canadian rules).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists under Canadian domestic law. The entity’s classification for Canadian tax is determined solely by corporate legal form. For US federal tax purposes, the ULC may file IRS Form 8832 to elect to be classified as a corporation, partnership, or disregarded entity. Canada also provides a section 216 ITA election for non-residents on Canadian rental income, and GST/HST elections for closely related corporations (e.g., section 156 election), but these do not alter the entity’s tax classification for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax). Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so the effective indirect tax rate is the federal 5% GST only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 (annual gross worldwide revenue of a small supplier from taxable supplies made in Canada; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded, regardless of whether the supply is a digital service or goods).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No government-mandated real-time fiscal clearance, API-based clearance, or digital stamping system exists in Canada. CRA accepts standard electronic invoices (B2B/B2C) provided they contain the prescribed information (supplier name and BN, invoice date, description of supply, GST/HST charged, and consideration). Registrants must retain invoices in an auditable format (e.g., PDF, CSV) and report GST/HST on a periodic return; there is no statutory requirement for a third-party digital clearinghouse.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of services are zero-rated under Section 9, Part V, Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act where the recipient is a non-resident of Canada and the supply is not in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property, and is not a service performed on or in relation to an individual in Canada. For the fleet route optimization and real-time telematics SaaS, the supply of cloud-based software services to foreign logistics operators (non-resident customers) qualifies for 0% GST/HST provided the customer is not a Canadian resident, the service is rendered outside Canada, and no basis exists for zero-rating denial under the place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (not applicable to pure services; required only if the supply includes physical goods – e.g., telematics hardware)
Bill of Lading (for goods shipments; for SaaS, a service agreement and server access log is the equivalent evidence)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or SWIFT/bank wire receipt from a non-resident account)
Written service agreement demonstrating non-resident customer status and offshore performance
Commercial invoice showing 0% GST/HST, referencing Section 9 of Schedule VI
Telematics platform usage logs or IP geolocation records evidencing the customer’s foreign location
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export within the normal four-year limitation period (or longer for misrepresentation) and require payment of any underpaid GST/HST plus interest and penalties. Under section 280.1 of the Excise Tax Act, penalties can reach up to 8% of the tax amount, and for willful or careless misstatements, penalties up to $25,000 and potential criminal charges under section 327 (including imprisonment). Refund claims lacking proper substantiation are denied and clawed back with retroactive interest. CRA’s audit focus includes cross-border digital service transactions; funds repatriated outside the 180-day window are scrutinized as indicators of no genuine export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Foreign-exchange policy and reserve administration are vested in the Minister of Finance and executed through the Exchange Fund Account, for which the Bank of Canada acts as fiscal agent. Prudential regulation of Schedule I banks is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46). Anti-money-laundering supervision, large-transaction reporting, and client due diligence are enforced by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). International economic sanctions are administered by Global Affairs Canada and enforced by the Canada Border Services Agency and the RCMP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Canada abolished exchange controls upon repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1952; the Canadian dollar trades freely without fixed parity, and there are no capital-account or current-account restrictions on CAD conversion, profit repatriation, service royalties, interest, or intercompany loan repayment. The Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation may open and operate CAD, USD, EUR, and other foreign-currency accounts without Bank of Canada approval. Practical remittance frictions are tax-led rather than FX-led: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5-15% under the Canada-U.S. Convention); Part XIV branch tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5% on the first CAD 500,000 of taxable income) where a U.S. shareholder treats the ULC as a disregarded entity and the ULC carries on business in Canada; and CRS/FATCA reporting. No convertibility certificate, foreign-investment exchange approval, or capital-import permit exists for a software export business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts; the ULC may retain export proceeds in CAD or foreign currency and may net them against payables in any currency. Residual obligations are statutory reporting only: (i) disclosure to the Canada Border Services Agency of any cross-border movement of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more under section 12 of the PCMLTFA and the Cross-border Currency and Monetary Instruments Reporting Regulations; (ii) bank-side FINTRAC reporting of electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more and large cash transactions; and (iii) CRA record retention proving the export character of software subscription income. Because fleet route optimization and telematics SaaS (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 488490) constitute services rather than physical goods, Customs Act export declarations and Export Control List licensing do not apply to the software.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional Medium as a secondary payments and FX collection rail; Not Viable as the primary treasury bank. Canada has no European-style EMI licence; cross-border digital payment providers operating into Canada must be registered as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and must satisfy provincial money-services requirements where applicable. Such entities (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex) may lawfully process cross-border collections, vendor disbursements, and currency conversion for the ULC, but they may not accept deposits in the bank-supervisory sense, are not members of Payments Canada, are not covered by the Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation, and cannot process payroll, GST/HST remittances, or CRA tax payments. The blueprint requires a Schedule I chartered-bank primary account with fintech rails layered on for collection efficiency and FX segmentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute mandates physical appearance, but bank policy commonly does. Most Schedule I banks permit fully remote onboarding for Canadian-resident directors through live video verification and a digitally notarized corporate identity package. Where the ULC has foreign (typically U.S.) shareholders or non-resident directors, enterprise AML policies typically require one of: (i) an in-person compliance interview at a corporate banking centre in Calgary or Edmonton; (ii) a notarized identity and signature package executed before a Canadian consular officer or qualified notary in the director's home jurisdiction, then couriered to the branch; or (iii) a bank-officer video interview plus appointment of one Canada-resident authorized signatory. The fastest lawful path for this ULC is to appoint one Canadian-resident director/signer at onboarding, execute a single video KYC session for the foreign UBO, and support the file with a consularized or notarized register extract from the Alberta Corporate Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation structure is flagged as an advanced-vehicle red flag because it is commonly used by U.S. investors for check-the-box tax planning and can obscure the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: (i) certified Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act with Corporate Access Number; (ii) Certificate of Status / Good Standing from the Alberta Corporate Registry; (iii) organizational chart identifying all UBOs at the 25% threshold; (iv) certified copy of the unanimous shareholder or members agreement; (v) notarized statutory declaration of UBO, source of funds, and source of wealth for each founder; (vi) for a U.S. shareholder, IRS Form 8832 election or a signed Canadian/U.S. tax opinion characterizing the ULC; (vii) beneficial-ownership register maintained under PCMLTFA Regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and foreign-issued identification trigger enhanced due diligence and may suspend onboarding pending EDD clearance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: (i) notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for each director or signatory (utility bill or bank statement less than three months old); (ii) completed bank EDD questionnaire; (iii) board resolution authorizing the signing matrix; (iv) 12-month cash-flow forecast and business plan for the Fleet Dispatch SaaS; (v) professional bank reference letter for each foreign shareholder; (vi) director profiles confirming commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Voluminous low-value inbound credits from Stripe Billing sweeps may be miscoded by transaction monitoring as unregulated money transmission or marketplace intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier required: (i) current Stripe merchant agreement and payout schedule demonstrating software-subscription revenue; (ii) read-only dashboard access or a structured settlement report; (iii) sample end-customer subscription contracts and invoices for fleet route optimization; (iv) internal GL mapping of Stripe batch settlements to operating revenue; (v) written confirmation that the ULC is not an MSB, holds no client funds, and processes no third-party payments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (ABCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary of incorporation (annual return date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 50 per annual return; failure to file for 5 consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve the ULC via strike-off under ABCA s. 208

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) record and directors' resolutions in the statutory minute book, including shareholder approval of financial statements and any auditor waiver
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretary / minute book maintained at the Alberta registered office (not filed with a regulator)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once each calendar year and no more than 15 months after the prior AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may face individual liability for actions not ratified by shareholders; inability to pass annual unanimous consents; persistent governance default becomes a factor in Registry compliance reviews

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate return reflecting the ULC's tax status and any Canada-U.S. Treaty pass-through election)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the ULC's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of any balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; continued non-filing can trigger CRA assumptions and director liability for unremitted source deductions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual with Significant Control (ISC) Register annual verification and Register of Directors update (verified against annual return data; no standalone UBO filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta registered office (subject to inspection by Service Alberta and authorized accessors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ISC changes recorded within 15 days of each change; register verified for accuracy on each annual return anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ABCA fines up to CAD 5,000 for failure to maintain or permit inspection of the ISC register; directors may be disqualified for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a non-distributing Alberta ULC: no revenue or asset threshold triggers a statutory audit. An auditor must be appointed at each AGM unless shareholders pass an annual unanimous resolution waiving audit, or the corporation is a distributing (public) issuer under ABCA. A transferable tax election (Canada-U.S. Treaty pass-through) does not relieve the accounting duty but does not itself mandate certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for distributing corporations; non-distributing private ULCs may prepare financial statements under Canadian ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) as an alternative to IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ABCA imposes a continuous ISC register obligation for each Individual with Significant Control; the ULC must keep particulars current at the registered office. There is no annual UBO form filed with Service Alberta: the annual return requires only current director and registered office information. Before each annual return date, the secretary must confirm ISC holdings, record any share transfers in the Register of Members, and ratify director and officer changes by board resolution.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with share transfer ledger)
Minute Book (AGM, board resolutions, and unanimous shareholder consents)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 - 380 per year (typical Alberta corporate registered office and registered agent service fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 18,000 yearly for a small logistics-technology SaaS entity when a full audit is required; USD 0 where shareholders execute the annual unanimous audit waiver
